name: Parcel delivery & couriers
one_line: Picks up packages and carries them to the door: the last mile of nearly everything bought online.
sells: Pickup, transport and last-mile delivery of parcels, priced per package by weight, speed and distance
customers: Online merchants, 3PLs and marketplaces shipping goods, plus businesses and consumers
suppliers: Trucks and aircraft, fuel, sortation and warehouse automation, and delivery labor and contractors

revenue.metric: U.S. parcel delivery revenue (total carrier spend)
revenue.basis: derived from Pitney Bowes (23.1B parcels x $9.34 revenue per parcel)
revenue.note: Pitney Bowes states 23.1B U.S. parcels in 2025 at $9.34 average revenue per parcel; the ~$216B is that product (both inputs are Pitney Bowes figures, the multiplication is ours). Carrier spend rose 6.2% in 2025. U.S. only: global parcel volume is far larger, led by China. UPS ($88.7B) and FedEx ($87.9B) are much bigger as companies because their totals include international and freight.

structure.type: Four-carrier oligopoly with a fast-growing fringe
structure.why: Four national networks carry ~92% of U.S. parcels. Amazon now leads by volume (its own packages), but UPS and FedEx still take ~62% of parcel revenue by carrying higher-value business and express shipments, while USPS anchors low-cost last-mile. A fringe of regional and last-mile carriers (OnTrac, Veho, UniUni) is the fastest-growing slice, lifted by Shein and Temu.
structure.hhi_note: Squared shares of the four listed carriers by 2025 U.S. parcel volume (Pitney Bowes) — moderately concentrated. By revenue the ranking reorders sharply: UPS 31.6%, FedEx 30.8%, Amazon 15.5%, USPS 14.9%, because Amazon's volume is low-value self-delivery while UPS and FedEx carry pricier B2B and express freight.

econ: Economies of density: the more parcels a carrier drops per route and per stop, the lower its cost per package, so dense national networks dominate and newcomers struggle to match their cost. The exception is vertical integration: a shipper with enough volume of its own, like Amazon, can build a captive delivery network and stop paying UPS and FedEx, which is why the market now splits into a volume leader (Amazon's own cheap packages) and the revenue leaders (UPS and FedEx carrying higher-value business and express shipments).

companies.name: Amazon Logistics
companies.share_basis: share of U.S. parcel volume in 2025, computed from Pitney Bowes stated volumes (6.9B of 23.1B)
companies.note: Amazon's in-house delivery arm; overtook USPS as the #1 U.S. parcel carrier by volume in 2025. It moves mostly Amazon's own low-value packages, so its ~15.5% revenue share trails its ~30% volume share; standalone revenue isn't disclosed.

companies.name: USPS
companies.share_basis: share of U.S. parcel volume in 2025, computed from Pitney Bowes stated volumes (6.2B of 23.1B)
companies.note: Government postal service; anchors low-cost last-mile and handles the final mile for other carriers. Parcel volume fell ~8.8% in 2025 as Amazon insourced; ~14.9% of U.S. parcel revenue. Total USPS revenue (~$80B) mostly comes from mail, not parcels.

companies.name: UPS
companies.share_basis: share of U.S. parcel volume in 2025, computed from Pitney Bowes stated volumes (4.3B of 23.1B)
companies.note: Leads U.S. parcel revenue (~31.6% of spend) despite ranking third by volume: focused on higher-value B2B and deliberately shedding low-margin Amazon volume. Total company revenue fell to $88.7B in 2025 (from $91.1B) and spans U.S. and international package plus supply chain.

companies.name: FedEx
companies.share_basis: share of U.S. parcel volume in 2025, computed from Pitney Bowes stated volumes (3.9B of 23.1B)
companies.revenue_display: $87.9B FY2025 total revenue (global, FY ended May 2025)
companies.note: Second by U.S. parcel revenue (~30.8%); merged Ground, Express and Services into one Federal Express segment ($75.3B of $87.9B total). Fiscal year ends May 31, so FY2025 revenue was roughly flat (+0.3%).

products_note: Flagship services as of Nov 2026; carrier volumes and shares from the Pitney Bowes Parcel Shipping Index 2026 report (2025 data), company revenue from UPS and FedEx earnings releases.
